maya: Quick heads-up — planning a short spike/ smoke for a hybrid kernel scheduling + KV eviction heuristic fit for both FlashAttention v2/v3. Want to validate that auto-selection doesn't regress streaming tail latency for long-chat workloads.

liam: SG. Do we have current baseline numbers to compare? p50/p95/p99 for token latency and kv miss rate?

bench-bot: Baseline (prod master, flashv2-only):
```
model: redwood/bison-13b
sequence: 1024
p50_token_latency: 12ms
p95_token_latency: 50ms
p99_token_latency: 190ms
kv_miss_rate: 0.6%
cost_per_token: $0.00085
```

sophia: Nice. For auto-selection, I'm proposing strategy: prefer flashv3 for short sequences (<512) and low-batch workloads, fall back to flashv2 when kv cache is hot (streaming with long context) or when flashv3 kernels show higher p99 on real traces.

nate: Concrete flag names? Also what about batching heuristics — we saw a regression when batch window was >20ms for flashv3.

maya: Draft flag: `ff_attn_kernel_strategy=hybrid:flashv3,flashv2,paged` with params:
```
selection_rules:
  - if avg_seq_len < 512 and batch_size < 8 -> flashv3
  - if kv_miss_rate > 1.0% -> flashv2
  - if batch_latency_ms > 35 -> paged
```
Canary plan: 3% nodes for 2 hours, watch p99 token latency, kv_miss_rate, cost_per_token.

liam: From profiling earlier today, flashv3 produced lower p50 but p99 climbed ~30% on streaming traces. We should capture per-shard kv eviction churn. Example trace log:
```
[2026-01-10 14:21:09] shard=7 kv_evict=23 kv_load=812 kv_hit_rate=98.5% avg_kv_latency=0.4ms
[2026-01-10 14:21:10] shard=7 kv_evict=118 kv_load=905 kv_hit_rate=89.3% avg_kv_latency=1.9ms
```

sophia: That suggests flashv3 pacing interacts badly with our KV cache prefetch policy. Quick mitigation: add soft cap on kv_eviction_per_sec per shard and increase `kv_prefetch_lookahead` for flashv3 paths.

maya: Proposed rollout checklist:
- Create feature flag `ff_flashmix_kernel_hybrid_v1` (ops owned)
- Canary 3% for 2h -> monitor dashboards: /d/redwood/attn-kernel-hybrid
- If p99 token latency > baseline * 1.25 OR kv_miss_rate increases > 0.5pp -> abort and rollback
- After 24h of stable canary -> ramp 10% -> 50% -> 100%

infra-bot: Deploy job scheduled: `deploy/attn-hybrid-canary` -> started 1751239950

liam: Also add metric `kv_eviction_churn` and a histogram for `token_generation_tail_ms` to the canary alert rule.

nate: For the smoke we should run both synthetic (bench harness) and a small replay of production traces (1k sessions). bench-bot can kick that off.

bench-bot: Kicking off: `bench/hybrid-smoke --replay=1k --duration=30m` -> results in ~30m. Link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abc123/attn-hybrid

sophia: If we see cost_per_token drop but kv_miss_rate increases, that's a sign batching/caching are masking the cost — don't auto-promote flashv3 without kv stability.

maya: Agreed. If canary passes, we'll add an A/B route test tied to `route_policy=latency_sensitive` so latency-sensitive customers stay on safer kernel. @nate please own the rollback playbook.

nate: On it. I'll prepare rollback script and runbook. :+1:

liam: ACK. I'll update the runtime fflags doc with the selection heuristic and metrics.

maya: Thanks all — will post a short post-canary summary in #eng-runtime. :rocket:
